Consequently, checkpoints specific to the raw cassette shell (two circular holes, write-protect tabs, dual spools) were correctly marked as 'false'. The Router did not skip any testable checkpoints; the only untestable one was the bottom opening due to perspective, which is a valid exclusion. The distinction between the device casing and the media itself is the primary alignment failure here.
artifact_review: The Router's artifact detection is strong. The 'structural_collapse' at the chain attachment (severity 3) is visually confirmed; the chain links merge into the plastic without a clear mechanical joint. The 'geometry_distortion' of the top handle (severity 2) is also valid, as it lacks functional symmetry. The topology expert's high mask confidence (0.99) indicates the object is segmented well as a whole, but this does not negate the local fusion artifacts at the chain connection point, which the Router correctly caught.
alignment_reasoning: Severe misalignment. The generated image is a 'cassette player' (Top-1 prediction by fine_grained_classifier), not a 'cassette' tape. While it shares a rectangular geometry, it fails all functional checkpoints specific to the tape media (spools, holes, tabs). The presence of gibberish text further degrades the semantic fidelity. Score is low but not zero because the object is recognizably related to the audio domain.
artifact_reasoning: Moderate to severe artifacts. Primary issue is text gibberish (severity 4) confirmed by OCR expert. Secondary issue is structural fusion at the chain attachment (severity 3) and minor geometric warping of the top handle (severity 2). The main body geometry is clean, preventing a catastrophic artifact score, but the details are flawed.
